help-home-step-1: At the top you see how much money you have.
help-home-step-2: Tap + to write down an expense or an income.
help-home-step-3: Below are your latest movements and your budgets.
help-home-step-4: Use the bar at the bottom to switch sections. On every screen, the ? button explains how it works.
help-home-tip: New here? Start by tapping + to write down your first expense.
help-add-transaction-title: How do I write down a movement?
help-add-transaction-step-1: Pick Expense if money went out, or Income if money came in.
help-add-transaction-step-2: Type the amount with the number pad.
help-add-transaction-step-3: Pick a category, like Food or Transport, so you know where the money goes.
help-add-transaction-step-4: Leave it on Normal if it already happened. The other options are for payments still to come.
help-transactions-title: How do I read my movements?
help-transactions-step-1: Here is everything you wrote down, newest first.
help-transactions-step-2: Expenses show in red and income in green.
help-transactions-step-3: Tap a movement to see or change it. Press and hold to pick several.
help-transactions-step-4: Use the search and filter buttons at the top to find something.
help-budgets-step-1: A budget is a limit: the most you want to spend in a period, for example $800,000 a month.
help-budgets-step-2: The bar fills up as you spend, so you see how much is left.
help-budgets-step-3: It can cover all your expenses or only some categories, like Food.
help-budgets-step-4: Tap + or the big button to create one.
help-budgets-tip: A budget helps you not overspend. Create one with what you want to spend this month.
help-pockets-step-1: An account is where your money is: your bank, Nequi or cash.
help-pockets-step-2: Inside each account you split the money into pockets: rent, savings, a trip...
help-pockets-step-3: "Free" is what you can spend without touching your pockets.
help-pockets-step-4: Tap a pocket to select it, and tap it again to see its movements. Use + to make a new one.
help-pockets-tip: Your money is organized in accounts (your bank, Nequi, cash) and, inside each one, in pockets.
help-pocket-title: How do I set up a pocket?
help-pocket-step-1: Give it a name that says what the money is for: Rent, Trip, Savings.
help-pocket-step-2: Pick a color so you spot it fast.
help-pocket-step-3: Choose which account it lives in, like your bank or Nequi.
help-pocket-step-4: If you're saving up, set a goal and a date, and the app shows how much is left.
help-more-step-1: Here are the tools, your pockets, the categories and the settings.
help-more-step-2: Tools has calculators and a chat to ask about your money.
help-more-step-3: In Settings you change the language and the colors, and make backups.
help-more-step-4: On any screen, the ? button explains how it works.
help-settings-step-1: Theme and style: the colors and dark mode.
help-settings-step-2: Language and format: the language, the currency and how numbers look.
help-settings-step-3: Import and export: save a copy of your data so you don't lose it if you change phones.
help-tools-step-1: Your money: your fixed payments and a chat to ask about your spending.
help-tools-step-2: Calculators: work out loans, interest rates and CDTs before you sign anything.
help-tools-step-3: Colombia: income tax, prima, cesantías and contributions for independent workers.
help-tools-step-4: The calculators don't change your accounts, so try any numbers you like.
help-tools-tip: Not sure where to start? Try the loan simulator and see what a loan really costs.
help-payments-title: How does the payments center work?
help-payments-step-1: At the top you see what your fixed payments add up to each month, like rent or Netflix.
help-payments-step-2: Tap a button like Rent or SOAT to create a reminder.
help-payments-step-3: Fill in the amount and the date. You get a notice before it's due.
help-payments-step-4: When you pay it, mark it as paid and it comes off your balance.
help-payments-tip: Add your fixed payments here and the app reminds you before each due date.
help-ai-chat-title: How do I turn on the chat?
help-ai-chat-step-1: The chat uses Gemini, Google's AI. It's free; you only need a Google account.
help-ai-chat-step-2: To connect it you need an API key: a long password that lets the app use Gemini for you.
help-ai-chat-step-3: Tap "Get my free key", sign in with Google and tap "Create API key". Then copy it.
help-ai-chat-step-4: Come back, paste it in the "Paste your key here" box and tap Save. Done, ask away!
help-account-title: How do I set up an account?
help-account-step-1: Write the name of your bank or wallet, for example Nequi.
help-account-step-2: Pick what kind it is: bank, digital wallet, cash, credit card or investment.
help-account-step-3: The 4x1000 is a tax of 4 pesos for every 1,000 that leave a bank. If your account charges it, the app writes it down for you.
help-account-step-4: Pick a color so you recognize it fast, then tap the button at the bottom.
help-income-tax-title: How do I use this calculator?
help-income-tax-step-1: Pick "With my transactions" to use what you wrote down, or "Calculator" to type the numbers yourself.
help-income-tax-step-2: Choose the year you're filing for.
help-income-tax-step-3: Fill in your income and what you can deduct. To see how it works first, tap the example button.
help-income-tax-step-4: At the end you see whether you have to file and about how much you'd pay. It's an estimate, not tax advice.

loan-disclaimer: This is a simulation with projected data; confirm the rate, installment and terms with your bank or lender before deciding.
loan-try-example-description: Fills in a motorcycle of $8.000.000 at 26% EA over 36 months so you can see how it works.
loan-guide-how-to-fill: How do I fill this in?
loan-guide-amount: Type how much they lend you, not the full price. If you give a down payment, subtract it first: a $10.000.000 motorcycle with $2.000.000 down is an $8.000.000 loan.
loan-rate-equivalent: Equals {ea} EA, or {mv} a month in arrears
loan-guide-rate-title: Where do I find the rate?
loan-guide-rate: Look in the offer or the simulator of your bank for "tasa efectiva anual (EA)". Offers often show a monthly rate (1,9% MV) because it looks lower; pick the matching type here and we convert it. To compare two loans, always compare the EA, and ask for the total cost with insurance included.
loan-guide-mv-ma-title: Monthly in arrears or in advance?
loan-guide-mv-ma: In arrears (MV) you pay the interest at the end of each month, which is the usual case. In advance (MA) the interest is charged at the start, so the same number costs more: 2% MA is about 2,04% MV. If the offer does not say, ask; we simulate both with their equivalent rate in arrears.
loan-guide-term: More months means a lower installment but more interest in total. Try 24 and 36 months with the same amount and compare the total paid.
loan-guide-system: Fixed installment: you pay the same every month; at first it is mostly interest. Constant principal: you pay the same principal every month plus the interest, so the first installments are higher and then drop, and you pay less interest overall.
loan-guide-fee-title: What are the life insurance and the handling fee?
loan-guide-fee: Most loans charge a life insurance (seguro de vida deudor) that pays the debt if something happens to you, and some charge a monthly handling fee. They are not interest but you pay them every month: ask for them and add them here to see the real installment.
loan-guide-extra-title: What does an extra payment do?
loan-guide-extra: An extra payment goes straight to the principal. You choose: reduce the term (same installment, you finish earlier, you save the most interest) or reduce the installment (same end date, smaller installments). Ask your bank which one it applies and whether it charges for it.
